[project]
name = "parcel-demo"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["ruff==0.14.3", "mypy==1.18.2"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = ["src/parcel_demo/generated"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "B", "I", "UP"]
ignore = ["F401"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
warn_unreachable = true
exclude = ["^src/parcel_demo/generated/"]
def greeting(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}"

structured_content.markdown: # Ruff ## First try **Illustrative example; not executed in this review.** [Install Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/installation/), then save this as `sample.py`: ```python import math print("Ready") ``` Run this in the directory containing the file. It checks for unused imports without changing the file or loading project configuration: ```sh ruff check --isolated --select F401 sample.py ``` Representative diagnostic excerpt, not captured output (formatting varies by version): ```text sample.py:1:8: F401 `math` imported but unused ``` The location identifies the import; `F401` identifies the unused-import rule. Remove that line and repeat the check. A clean result means this selected rule found no violation in this file. ## Use it on your project Follow the [Ruff tutorial](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/tutorial/) to configure rule selection, file exclusions, and the target Python version. Run `ruff check` for linting; `ruff format` only formats code. Start without automatic fixes so you can inspect the diagnostics. ## Fixes and limitations Ruff distinguishes safe and unsafe fixes. Review proposed changes and run your tests after applying them. Record the tool version, configuration, and preview setting for repeatable results. ## Alternatives and complements Follow the [Ruff and mypy recipe](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/python-checks/) to check one project with separate lint and type reports. Pair Ruff with [mypy](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/mypy/) or [Pyright](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/pyright/) when you also need type checking. Consider [Bandit](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/bandit/) for a dedicated Python security-rule workflow. [Pylint](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/pylint/) uses inference and supports plugins; Ruff provides built-in rule families. Their rules overlap but are not interchangeable. Before switching, compare the diagnostics and plugin requirements of your project. The [official comparison](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/faq/#how-does-ruffs-linter-compare-to-pylint) explains these differences. Use the [finding review workflow](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/reviewing-findings/) to investigate a diagnostic and verify a correction.

structured_content.markdown: # mypy ## Where it fits Use mypy to check whether code uses the types described by annotations and stubs consistently. It complements [Ruff](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/ruff/) for linting and [Bandit](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/bandit/) for selected Python security patterns. A clean lint run is not a type-checking result. Gradual typing lets a project adopt annotations in stages. By default, bodies of functions without annotations receive limited checking. `Any` and ignored imports can also let type mistakes pass unnoticed. ## First try **Illustrative example, not run here.** Follow the [mypy installation instructions](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/getting_started.html) in your selected Python environment, then save this as `sample.py`: ```python def next_count(count: int) -> int: return count + 1 next_count("three") ``` Check it without running the program: ```sh python -m mypy sample.py ``` Representative diagnostic, not captured output (formatting varies by version): ```text sample.py:4: error: Argument 1 to "next_count" has incompatible type "str"; expected "int" [arg-type] ``` `sample.py:4` locates the call. `arg-type` identifies an incompatible argument type: text was passed to an integer parameter. Replace the argument with `3` and check again. This example exercises one mismatch, not the entire type system. See the [argument-type diagnostic reference](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/error_code_list.html#check-argument-types-arg-type) for details. Use the [shared Ruff and mypy recipe](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/python-checks/) for a pinned environment, faulty/corrected files, and separate reports. ## Configure a useful check Supply the project's imports and any required third-party stubs. Start with a small annotated area, inspect errors, and tighten the configuration deliberately. `--check-untyped-defs` can inspect unannotated bodies, while `--strict` enables a broader set of checks. Record the mypy version, configuration, target Python version, and suppressions. Static types do not validate arbitrary input data at runtime or replace application tests. [Compare mypy, Ruff, and Bandit](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/compare/?tools=tools%2Fmypy%2Ctools%2Fruff%2Ctools%2Fbandit) to see their different roles. ## Compare Python type checkers [Pyright](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/pyright/) is another Python type checker. Both use annotations and stubs, but configuration, inference, diagnostics, and plugin support differ. For a useful trial, check the same revision with matching Python version, platform, imports, and intended strictness. Investigate disagreements instead of comparing diagnostic counts. Keep [mypy import and stub settings](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/running_mypy.html) and [Pyright settings](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) with the reports. [Compare mypy and Pyright](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/compare/?tools=tools%2Fmypy%2Ctools%2Fpyright). Ruff remains complementary for lint rules; running two type checkers is a deliberate evaluation choice, not a requirement of the Python recipe.

item.text:
Start with Ruff, then mypy, using your existing configuration for both.

| Tool | What it checks | Fit for this project |
|---|---|---|
| [Ruff](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/ruff/) | Common mistakes and coding conventions | Already configured for error rules, Pyflakes, bugbear, import sorting, and Python modernization |
| [mypy](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/mypy/) | Consistency of annotations, arguments, returns, and operations | Your code has annotations, and strict checking plus unreachable-code warnings are already enabled |

Your `pyproject.toml` pins Ruff `0.14.3` and mypy `1.18.2`, targets Python 3.12, and excludes `src/parcel_demo/generated/` from discovery in both tools. Ruff deliberately ignores `F401` (unused imports).

From the current directory, with those pinned tools installed in your Python 3.12 environment, run:

```powershell
python -m ruff check src
python -m mypy --config-file pyproject.toml src
```

These commands retain the configured rules, strictness, target versions, and exclusions. Start by reviewing Ruff's findings, then examine mypy's type errors. No additional rules or stricter flags are needed for the initial baseline. Avoid Ruff's `--select`, which replaces configured rule selection, and `--isolated`, which bypasses project configuration.

The tools complement each other: Ruff does not replace type checking, and mypy can miss problems hidden by `Any`, missing stubs, or suppressions. Neither replaces runtime tests. See the linked ToolWiki profiles above.

I only inspected files and consulted ToolWiki; I did not run analyzers or edit files. This is documentation-based guidance, not an execution result.
